newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end lower ahead of Soffex expiry.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end lower ahead of Soffex expiry.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower on Thursday as the market grew nervous ahead of Friday's expiry of July contracts on Soffex.
"There was selling pressure from SMI futures, which led to high volatility," one dealer said.
He said he expected the market to continue in the same manner on Friday. "It's possible that we lose another 50 points tomorrow."
But another trader said the general outlook remained good. "Fundamentals have not changed and a cooling off after the recent rally is most welcome," he said.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 59.2 points or 1.0 percent to 5,868.3 points.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 25.36 points or 0.69 percent at 3,704.95.
Bourse volume stood at 2.92 billion francs.
Nestle, which said half-year sales figures rose 17.5 percent to 33.5 billion Swiss francs, was one of the biggest losers. The shares slumped 42 francs to 1,927.
Dealers said the growth rate was somewhat disappointing and noted the company also said it expected sales growth to slow in the second half.
Novartis led the actives list, dropping 21 francs to 2,420.
Roche certificates, which saw strong gains in the past few sessions, slipped 195 francs to 14,615.
ABB was up 10 francs to 2,130. "The stock looks good for technical reasons," one trader said.
Sulzer Medica, which started trading on Monday for the first time, continued to move up, adding 5.5 francs to 440.

Shares of Sulzer AG, the company that spun off Sulzer Medica, ended two francs lower at 1,215. Sulzer chief executive Fritz Fahrni said in a newspaper interview that group net profit could more than double this year.
